ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the beaker on the left is labeled Solution A, with the volume beside it labeled 500. mL, and the concentration below the beaker labeled 0.350 M calcium hydroxide. On the right there is also Solution B, labeled 300. mL and ??? M calcium hydroxide, but this question asks about the amount of calcium hydroxide dissolved to prepare Solution A. Then reason: The amount dissolved in the question is calculated here by mass. Convert the volume of Solution A, 500 mL, to 0.500 L. The amount of substance n = M × V = 0.350 mol/L × 0.500 L = 0.175 mol. The molar mass of Ca(OH)2 is approximately 40.08 + 2(16.00 + 1.008) = 74.09 g/mol. Mass m = n × molar mass = 0.175 mol × 74.09 g/mol = 12.97 g.
